title: Taxes, subsidies & price controls
examples: What is the difference between a tax and a subsidy?
How does a minimum price affect the market?
Can you explain the concept of tax incidence with an example?

explain.say: Today we will look at how governments change prices. We will study taxes, subsidies, and price controls.
Tax incidence shows who actually pays the tax. It is not always the person who pays the tax directly.
A minimum price, or price floor, sets a lowest legal price. This is often used to support workers.
When the minimum price is set above equilibrium, a surplus occurs. This means too much of the good is available.
A maximum price, or price ceiling, sets a highest legal price. This is often used to protect consumers.
In real life, think about rent control laws. These are maximum prices set by the government.

faq.q: If a government imposes a tax, does the buyer always pay more?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Tax incidence means the burden can fall on either the buyer or the seller, depending on their relative elasticities.
asks: Does the seller always absorb the tax cost?

faq.q: What happens if the minimum price is set too high?
faq.a: If the minimum price is above the market equilibrium, it creates a surplus because sellers are forced to sell above what buyers are willing to pay.
asks: What is a surplus at a price floor?
Will a high minimum price cause problems?

faq.q: Are price ceilings always good for consumers?
faq.a: Not always. While they protect buyers from high prices, they can lead to shortages because suppliers are discouraged from producing the good.
asks: What are the downsides of rent control?

faq.q: How do subsidies affect the market?
faq.a: Subsidies effectively lower the cost of production for a good, which shifts the supply curve outwards and lowers the market price paid by consumers.
asks: What is the effect of a subsidy?

faq.q: Is a price floor the same as a minimum wage?
faq.a: Yes, the minimum wage is a common example of a minimum price, or a price floor, set for labor.
asks: Is minimum wage a price control?
What is the minimum wage an example of?

facts: A tax increases the cost for producers or consumers.
A subsidy decreases the cost for producers or consumers.
A minimum price (price floor) must be above equilibrium to have an effect.
A maximum price (price ceiling) must be below equilibrium to have an effect.

quiz.say: If the government sets a minimum price for wheat above the market equilibrium, what will happen?

options.show: A shortage of wheat will occur.
options.say: A shortage of wheat will occur.

options.show: The market will adjust back to equilibrium.
options.say: The market will adjust back to equilibrium.

options.show: The tax incidence will be zero.
options.say: The tax incidence will be zero.

options.show: A surplus of wheat will occur.
options.say: A surplus of wheat will occur.

quiz.why: Because the minimum price is higher than the natural market price, suppliers will produce and sell more than consumers are willing to buy.

wrong.0: This is wrong because a shortage happens when the price is set too low.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the government price control prevents the natural market clearing process.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the price control itself is a direct intervention affecting supply and demand.

quiz.say: A subsidy given to solar panel manufacturers will most likely cause:

options.show: No change in the market price.
options.say: No change in the market price.

options.show: An increase in the supply of solar panels.
options.say: An increase in the supply of solar panels.

options.show: A decrease in the demand for solar panels.
options.say: A decrease in the demand for solar panels.

options.show: A higher market price for solar panels.
options.say: A higher market price for solar panels.

quiz.why: Subsidies lower the cost of production, making it cheaper for manufacturers to supply more panels at any given price.

wrong.0: Subsidies always shift the supply curve, causing a measurable price change.
wrong.2: This confuses the effect of a subsidy, which affects supply, not consumer desire.
wrong.3: Subsidies are designed to lower costs, not raise them.

quiz.say: If the price of gasoline is legally capped below the equilibrium price, what is the most likely immediate result?

options.show: The price will immediately rise to the equilibrium level.
options.say: The price will immediately rise to the equilibrium level.

options.show: A shortage of gasoline will develop.
options.say: A shortage of gasoline will develop.

options.show: The sellers will absorb all the cost of the cap.
options.say: The sellers will absorb all the cost of the cap.

options.show: The market will simply ignore the price cap.
options.say: The market will simply ignore the price cap.

quiz.why: When the price is artificially kept too low, the quantity demanded will exceed the quantity supplied.

wrong.0: The government enforcement prevents the price from naturally rising to clear the market.
wrong.2: While sellers are affected, the primary market outcome is the shortage, not just the cost absorption.
wrong.3: Legally enforced price controls are binding and change market behaviour.
